The company-authored September 3, 2026 offering statement estimates approximately 7 acres per day per robot and specifies cutting when weeds reach 3–5 inches, with a 60-inch turn zone for the main field, endrows and obstacles. These are estimates under optimal conditions, not independently verified guarantees.

Each robot uses the GreenTRIP RTK system for field mapping and autonomous navigation with a 15 km range radius and centimeter-level accuracy, plus onboard cameras with human-detection algorithms and geofencing.

Greenfield reports a 2025 leased fleet of 23 robots across seven states and 70 orders for 2026 delivery (48 purchase, 22 lease), with 60 robots shipped as of June 4, 2026. It operates made-to-order without maintaining robot inventory.

The robots are remotely monitored through the Operator software, and the Fleet Manager agent is described as coordinating fleets of 10 or more robots on fields of 300+ acres. Performance remains an issuer estimate subject to battery, terrain, crop and weather conditions.

highlights: Hai Robotics describes HaiPick as an award-winning goods-to-person automation system and lists four base systems: HaiPick Climb, System 1, System 2 and System 3.

The company claims 3x throughput, 4x efficiency, 67% lower labor costs, 75% reduced storage footprint and 99%+ order-picking accuracy for HaiPick systems. These are supplier claims, not independent benchmarks.
The A42T-E2 is presented as a second-generation telescopic ACR with a single-hook Chain-Pick system that can haul three interlocking totes and carry eight in its tray tower.
